implementation: Dense CPU reference BEM -> full T matrix -> analytic uniform SO(3) average of all 16 Mueller elements
online_timing_scope: A single timed execution per case; compares averaging after the same T matrix has already been built, not total BEM runtime.
BEM_error_scope: The coarse sphere has about 3% Mueller error vs Mie. Centered tetrahedron ref=2 has about 2.6% energy-balance error. These surface errors are independent of T truncation and SO(3) integration.

cost_model.formula: T = D A^-1 B; q=2 L (L+2). Direct baseline uses 2 M independent plane-wave RHS after alpha and particle symmetries.
cost_model.break_even: q*c_modal_solve + T projection + analytic averaging < 2*M*c_plane_solve + direct farfield averaging
cost_model.geometry: regular six-sided prism H/D=1, equal-volume radius 1
cost_model.estimate_limit: Heuristic starting orders, not accuracy guarantees. Estimate uses circumscribed radius kR; material resonances and target accuracy require convergence checks.

validation: 5 Python tests passed: generic complex SO(3) cubature, vector-harmonic orthonormality, Mie convention, Clebsch coefficients, integrated Mueller vs scattering trace
C++ radiation operator checked independently against muller_nodal_farfield
Direct BEM reconstruction checked at incident and outgoing directions excluded from T projection quadrature
limitations: CPU and small-order reference only (L <= 8); no production FMM backend or measured GPU end-to-end T speedup
Current dense bridge material is real refractive index, nonmagnetic exterior
Reference irreducible-block contraction is not optimized for large L
Full T construction is not automatically cheaper than existing symmetry-reduced adaptive orientation solves
